summary: Feed s164_triple is degraded: 3 faults found. VLANs 10,20 stripped (100% untagged), IDS port overloaded by 3.53 Gbps bursts on 1 Gbps port (353% capacity), and 75.7% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance, limiting payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery. All packets arrived untagged yet IDS requires VLANs 10 and 20, indicating broker VLAN handling set to strip or access-port SPAN not forwarding trunk tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot classify or apply VLAN-aware policies for VLAN 10 and 20; traffic appears as single flat network, causing missed detections and incorrect segmentation for those tenants.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10,20 through the TAP/SPAN and packet broker so IDS receives correctly tagged traffic for policy enforcement.

findings.root_cause: Bursty aggregate traffic (3.53 Gbps peak in 1ms) is being sent to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load balancing or shaping. Broker is not distributing load across multiple tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffer overrun and packet drops during bursts; IDS misses flows and signatures, creating detection gaps despite needing both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic with packet-broker load balancing (or upgrade tool port to 10G) to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops.

findings.root_cause: 75.7% of bytes are TLS/encrypted, above the IDS 60% tolerance. No upstream SSL visibility/decryption is applied, so broker forwards opaque payloads the IDS cannot inspect.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection but cannot analyze encrypted payloads, reducing detection coverage to metadata only and missing encrypted exploits/C2.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective TLS decryption at the packet broker/SSL visibility appliance or feed decrypted copy plus metadata to IDS to restore payload visibility within tolerance.
